title: Investigate and remediate cross-region TTFT surge caused by preemptive GPU context reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Over the last 36 hours several customers (hosted + dedicated + private) reported sudden TTFT regressions and tokens/sec drops across multiple models and regions. Initial triage indicates a correlation with our proactive GPU context reclamation heuristic that runs during low-util windows and triggers for workers with fragmented KV caches. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, short-term fix, and a rollout plan for the durable patch to the runtime scheduler and prefetch logic.
repro_steps: 1) Replay customer traffic pattern via perf-replay with 75% short-session, 25% long-session mix at 3x normal concurrency
2) Enable context-reclaim feature toggle in staging (feature=context_reclaim_staged=true)
3) Observe that workers with >1MB cumulative KV state are scheduled for reclamation during low-util windows
4) Send mixed-model fanout (gpt-*-like + quantized-int8) to same slot and measure first token latency and tokens/sec over 2 minute window
investigation:
- Correlated 99th and p95 TTFT spikes with reclamation events recorded in telemetry (worker.event=context_reclaim_start/context_reclaim_done).
- KV cache eviction during reclamation caused warm caches to be dropped forcing model re-warm, increasing kernel selection time and memory copies.
- Affected variants are quantized int8 + mixed-sparse variants where kernel selection heuristics degrade after eviction.
- Private deployments with aggressive host-level cgroup OOM policies amplified the impact because reclaimed GPUs entered OS-level memory compaction and paused processes briefly.
- Multi-region incidents show propagation: once a region experiences reclaimed-worker thrash, smart-router attempts capacity failover and floods adjacent regions, worsening tokens/sec across the fleet.
mitigation_actions: 1) Immediately disable proactive context_reclaim in hosted and dedicated control plane (feature flag rollback) — PROD change deployed 2026-03-08 22:10 UTC
2) For Private customers, send a targeted advisory to operators with an opt-out KB and suggested systemd/cgroup tuning to defer kernel-level reclamation
3) Route critical customer traffic to warm-pool instances that pin KV caches while we stabilize (manual routing policy applied for affected customers)
4) Short-term scheduler guard: avoid reclaiming workers with cumulative KV cache > 512KB and active recent-access rate > 10 req/min (temporary heuristic)
fix_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): adjust scheduler to include model-variant-aware reclaim thresholds and skip on high-eviction-cost variants — target patch in runtime-1.19-rc (estimate 2 days)

Phase 2 (robust): add reclamation hysteresis and telemetry enrichment (worker.eviction_cost_estimate), implement prefetch quick-rewarm path for KV cache that preserves compressed checkpoints — target runtime-1.19 GA (estimate 2 sprints)

Phase 3 (deploy): canary rollout to non-critical regions for 48h with automatic rollback on >10% p95 TTFT delta. Post-rollout, enable gradual ramp to all regions with release notes and runbook updates.
rollback_plan: If p95 TTFT increases >15% during canary or customers report new regressions, immediately flip feature flag to remove the new reclaim logic and re-route affected customers to warm-pool. Maintain hotfix branch for rapid emergency 1-line revert. Notify SRE and Customer Success channels and open incident conference bridge.
